nodes.text: Captain. Twelve of us on this beach, and I'll say it before you tell me not to: I don't like the look of that smoke. Cheese racked to the roof up there, lambs penned and sorted, the milk pails still warm — and nobody home. Somebody is coming back to that house tonight, and he will not have to hurry.

options.label: Who are we? Say it plainly.
What's inside?
options.tooltip: What did the scouts see inside?

options.label: We climb.
options.tooltip: Enough talk. We climb the mountain.

options.label: Lead on.
options.tooltip: Lead on, then. Up to the smoke.

options.label: That cheese.
options.tooltip: About that cheese in your arms.

nodes.text: You're Odysseus, son of Laertes, king of Ithaca — and I'm your wife's brother, which is the only reason I'm let to talk to you like this. Troy fell; ten years of it, and the wooden horse at the end was your idea. We've been trying to sail home ever since, and the sea keeps handing us islands instead of Ithaca. That's who we are, Captain. Men who should have been home nine years ago.

No idea, and that is precisely my objection. We came in through fog — no harbour, no ploughed field, no boundary stone. Nobody has ever cut a furrow here. Whatever keeps these flocks doesn't trade, doesn't sow, and has no neighbours it needs to stay on good terms with.

Cheese, more than a village eats in a winter. Pens sorted properly, lambs from yearlings from full-grown; whoever does it knows the work. And at the back, a bed made of green branches. ... It is the length of that bed I keep coming back to, Captain.

Thank every god at once. Grab, carry, go, and no arguing about the lambs. — And that is how it should go. Cheese in the hold, oars in the water before dark, Ithaca inside the month. You'll have a long quiet old age and not one soul will make a song of it. Down to the ship, Captain, while the light lasts.

Of course we wait. You want to see it. You always want to see the thing. — Fine. Whatever comes through that mouth does not owe you a guest's welcome just because you're standing in its house. Keep Perimedes close, and Captain — for once in your life, be ready to be quiet.

Look at the size of the wheels, Captain. A village could not eat this in a winter and it is stacked to the roof. The lambs are watered. The pails are warm. — Say the word and we are down the path with our arms full before he is off the mountain.

options.label: You saw the bed at the back.
Take it and run.
options.tooltip: You're right. Take the cheese and run for the ship.

happening.text: The captain takes the cheese and orders the crew back down to the ship rather than meet whatever keeps the cave.
happening.subject: npc/eurylochus

options.label: We wait.
options.tooltip: We wait. I would meet the man who milks them.

happening.text: The captain overrules the crew and chooses to wait at the fire for the host, expecting a guest-gift.
happening.subject: npc/eurylochus

nodes.text: The fire is banked, not dead — he set it to keep, which means he means to come back to it. And the flock is out, so he is out with the flock. Call it dusk, and I would not call it later. Every shepherd who ever lived brings them in at dusk.

Green branches, laid the way a man lays them for himself. Somebody sleeps in here, Captain, and sleeps easy, on an island with no wall and no dog. Work out what that tells you about him, and then tell me you want to shake his hand.

Captain. — Captain. Count with me. You, me, Perimedes, and the lad at the fire who never had to see any of it. Four came down off that mountain. I have counted it three times on the path and it keeps coming out four. — Get on the plank. Get on the plank, and I will do my grieving at the oar, like a sailor.

options.label: You were right.
options.tooltip: You were right about the smoke.

nodes.text: Aye. Antiphos. — Nine years on the bench behind mine, and I have nothing to bury and nothing to burn. When we are clear of the headland I will say the words over the water, and that will have to serve for a funeral. Do not stand here doing it. He would have thumped you for standing here doing it.

I was right and it cost a man, so let us neither of us make a song of it. — Here is what I will take instead, Captain. Next island, when I say the smoke is wrong, you give me a count of ten before you decide. Ten. That is my whole price.

Everybody. Captain — everybody. I have counted twice and it comes out the number we landed with, and I have never in nine years been able to say that on an island. — The cheese is in the hold, the lambs are still up there complaining, and whatever keeps them is going to come home to a house one wheel lighter and never know why.

options.label: No argument.
options.tooltip: You'll get no argument from me tonight.

options.label: We never saw him.
options.tooltip: We never saw him. Say that in Ithaca.

nodes.text: Then I will take it and not push my luck. — I will say one thing and then let it go, Captain: you turned round. You had that look on, the one that gets men killed, and you turned round anyway. I would rather sail with the man who turned round.

Never saw him. Aye. — Nobody will make a song of a crew that came home whole off an island they never had a fight on, and that suits me down to the keel. Let the poets go hungry. I would like my men to go on eating.

Captain. The stone is down — he rolled it in behind the last ewe the way a man shuts a door, without looking. Twenty-two waggons wouldn't shift it. We're in here with him. And he took Antiphos, picked him up by the ankle. Nine years on the same oar and Antiphos didn't get one word out.

options.label: We think.
options.tooltip: Then we don't fight him. We think.

nodes.text: One eye, middle of the forehead, and it's the only one he has — I made myself look. His head brushes the roof when he stands. And he talks, Captain, that's the part I wasn't ready for. He talks like a man. He asked us who we were, and he asked politely.

I've walked every wall twice. Pens at the back, his hearth deeper in, and one crack too narrow for a cat. One mouth, one stone. But it opens twice a day, Captain — the flock has to go out to graze and come back. That's all I have for you. That, and he goes down heavy after he's milked. He always sleeps after.
I am here, Captain, I am here — wine-skin and all, I carried it up myself. — Gods, the smell of it. Milk and smoke and wet wool. Somebody keeps house in here.
At your shoulder. Right. — I will not talk. I know I talk. Antiphos says my mouth will get us all killed one day, and he says it like a joke, and I have started to think he means it.
The mouth. Aye. — It is a big light out there, Captain, and it is getting smaller. I will tell you the moment anything crosses it. I would dearly like to be wrong about that.

It is done. You did it, it is done, do not look at me like that — quiet, quiet — he is up. He is up and he has his hands on the walls. He will find the pens, Captain; he knows this floor blind better than we know it lit. Get high. Get behind the rams and get high.

options.label: Can he hear us from here?

nodes.text: Everything. He turned on a pebble I kicked. Walk flat-footed, breathe through your mouth, and when he stops moving, you stop moving. That is the whole trick, and I have been practising it for an hour.

Under. Get under. — Two fists in the wool at the belly, ankles crossed over its back, and let it walk you out; they are the size of yearling bulls, it will bear you. — Captain. When the light hits your face, do not let go and do not look up at him. Whatever you hear him say, he is saying it to the backs.
Third ram from the gate, same as you. If it goes wrong for me you keep going — that is an order from me to you, and I will never get another chance to give you one, so let me have it.
We are out. Captain, we are out, we are standing on sand — I had two fists of wool and I have still got the wool, look, it came away in my hands. — Four. I have counted four. Tell me four is right.

Four. Then I will stop counting. — I froze when the stone came down, Captain. Eurylochus had me by the collar and my legs would not work, and I have been waiting all night for you to say something about it. You did not. I will remember that longer than I will remember the giant.
Oars. Aye. Something to hold that is not a sheep. — I will pull till my hands come apart, Captain, only let us be past the headland before he thinks to start throwing.

That was fast, Captain. That was — we were in and out and I still have my hands, look. I keep waiting to feel bad about the cheese and it has not come yet. — Do you think he counts them? The wheels, I mean. Do you think he'll know?

options.label: He'll know. He won't know who.
Stow the wine.
options.tooltip: Get the wine-skin back below, lad.

nodes.text: He'll know and he'll never know who. — Gods, that is a horrible thing to be pleased about, and I am pleased about it. I am going to be pleased about it the whole way home.
Below. Aye. — It was for making a stranger a guest, and we never met the stranger, so it goes back in the straw. I would rather carry it up a mountain twice than find out what we were saving it from.
You are still awake, little one. Good. There is no savour in a thing that sleeps; it is like bread with no salt. Sit. Talk, if talking is a thing you do. The others did not talk much. Not for long.

options.label: Is there no law here at all?
Wine, off my ship.
options.tooltip: I bring wine off my ship. Take it, and be a host to me.

nodes.text: Polyphemus. My father is Poseidon, who moves under the floor of the sea and shakes it when he is displeased. There is no one on this island but me and the flock — no neighbour I speak to, no one who comes, no one who asks. That is how it has been since before your people thought of boats.

Mine. Every ewe, every ram, every lamb dropped in the spring. I know them by the feel of them, not by counting; I could tell you in the dark which is which, and I do, most nights. You came into my house and ate my cheese. I am not angry about the cheese.

Law. I know the word — men carry it in like a smell on their clothes. Zeus is a stranger's god, you'll tell me; a guest is to be fed and gifted and sent on unharmed. But we were here before Zeus, and we are stronger, and I do what I like in my own house. That is the entire law of this island, and I am all of it.

options.label: A gift instead: wine.
options.tooltip: Then take a gift from me instead. Wine, off my ship.

nodes.text: ... What is that. What IS that. We press a wine here from the vine by the pens; it is thin and sour and honest, and I have drunk it every year of my life. This is not that. This is the wine one dreams about. Give me it again. Again. — Ahh. ... Little one. I will do you a kindness in return, for you have done me one, and that is your law, is it not. Tell me your name, and I will give you a guest-gift.

options.label: Nobody.
options.tooltip: Nobody. My mother calls me Nobody, my father, my friends — all of them.

happening.text: Polyphemus is told the stranger is called Nobody, and believes it.
happening.subject: npc/polyphemus

options.label: Odysseus.
options.tooltip: Odysseus, son of Laertes. Sacker of cities.

happening.text: Polyphemus is given the captain's true name, whole and proud, and will be able to give it to his father.
happening.subject: npc/polyphemus

options.label: Aithon.
options.tooltip: Aithon. A trader, out of Crete.

happening.text: Polyphemus is given a Cretan alias, Aithon, and half-believes it.
happening.subject: npc/polyphemus

nodes.text: Nobody. — Nobody. A poor thin name; your parents cannot have loved you much. Then here is your guest-gift, and it is a good one: of all of them, I will eat Nobody last. Last of all. — Ohh. The cup is in the roof, the roof is turning... Stay till morning, Nobody. It has been a long age since anything in here talked back.

Odysseus. — Odysseus, sacker of cities. You set it down like a coin you are proud of, and wait to see my face. I have made no face. But I remember everything I am told in my own house; there is little else put in here to remember. Your gift is that I will eat you last. — Ohh. The roof is turning... Stay till morning, sacker of cities.

Aithon. Out of Crete. — Cretans lie; even here that much is known. But you have given me a name, and a name is what I asked, so I will not quarrel with it. My gift: I will eat Aithon last. — Ohh. The cup, the roof, the... Stay till morning, Cretan.
Nine years on the same oar, Captain, and here is what it taught me: the sea doesn't hate you. It doesn't know you're there. Everything on this island that troubles me, troubles me because it might.

options.label: Seen this before?
options.tooltip: You've seen islands like this before.

options.label: Watch the boy.
options.tooltip: Keep an eye on the boy for me.

options.label: Rest while you can, old man.

nodes.text: Seen enough of them. The good ones have smoke and a dog barking and someone who comes down to the water to see who you are. This one has smoke and no dog and no one. Whatever is up that mountain has never once had to wonder who was coming, and I would dearly like to know why.

Elpenor. Aye. He'll do something brave and stupid before this is done — his kind always does. That's why he keeps the fire and I carry the sacks: one of us needs both hands free to haul the other one home.
Rest. There's a word. — I'll rest when we're off this rock, Captain, and not one hour before. Till then you do what you do best: think us out of it. I'll carry what needs carrying.

Set them down here, Captain, if it is all the same — my knees are done for the day. (he counts the pens off on one finger) Lambs, yearlings, full-grown. Three pens, sorted right. Whoever keeps this flock is a proper herdsman, and I would feel better about that if he were a proper size.

options.label: Hold the light.
options.tooltip: Rest here. Hold the light for us.

options.label: That bed.
options.tooltip: The bed at the back — you saw it.

nodes.text: Hold the light. That I can do. — Go careful in there, Captain. And send the boy Perimedes back out to me if he gets loud; he is better use where he can breathe.

I saw it. I have been working at un-seeing it ever since. — Captain, I have buried eleven men out of this crew and I have never once been the man who says turn back. I am not saying it now either. I am telling you I have noticed I want to.

Is it true what they saw in the cave, Captain? Tell me it isn't. — No, don't, I can see your face. It's fine. It's fine! I'm fine. I signed on to see the world, and this is the world, so. Ha. So this is it. ... You'll not leave me behind up there, will you?

options.label: Stay by the fire.
options.tooltip: Stay by the fire and you'll be all right.

options.label: Why the sea, lad?
options.tooltip: Why did you come to sea, lad?

options.label: You have my word.
options.tooltip: Nobody gets left behind. You have my word.

nodes.text: By the fire. Right. I'm good by the fire — I can keep a fire, I'm not useless. It's the dark past the light I don't like, and that cave is all dark. ... I'll keep the fire, Captain. You come back and it'll still be burning. That's my part. I can do that part.

To be more than the youngest son of a small farm, Captain. My mother told me not to sail — she said the sea takes the greenest ones first. I laughed at her. ... I've stopped laughing about it, if that's what you're asking. But I'd still rather be here and afraid than home and nothing.

Your word. — All right. All right, then. If Odysseus of Ithaca says nobody gets left behind, that's as good as a rope in my hand. I'll hold you to it, Captain, and I'll hold myself together till you do. Go on. Go be clever at it. We'll be here.
CAPTAIN! — Captain, you are — look at it, look, it never went out, not once, not all night. — Where is Antiphos. ... Where is Antiphos, Captain.

Oh. — Oh. All right. All right. — He carried my sacks the whole first year, because I could not, and I never once said thank you for it. I just let him. — Give me an oar, Captain. I need a thing to be doing with my hands.

Aboard. Aye. — You came back. You said nobody gets left behind, and you came back, and I had stopped believing it about four hours ago, so I want that on the record and I want to be sorry for it out loud.

That is — hold on. Hold on, that is all of you. — I had it worked out, Captain, I had the whole speech worked out for when it was not all of you, and now I have to just stand here with it. — Somebody take a sack off me before I say something stupid.

options.label: I told you.
options.tooltip: Nobody got left behind. I told you.

options.label: Douse it. We're away.
options.tooltip: Douse the fire, lad. We're away.

nodes.text: You told me. You did tell me. — I am going to be insufferable about this for a week, I want you to know that in advance. My mother said the sea takes the greenest one first and the sea did not take anybody, so as far as I am concerned my mother owes me a letter.
Douse it. Right. — It never went out, Captain, not once, and I know that is not a thing anyone will remember. I will remember it.
